description.narrative: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended by the World Health Organisation for the first six months of life, because of benefits to mother and child. However, worldwide around half of all women require treatment with some form of medication during breastfeeding. For all mothers, their first concern will be about potential consequences to the infant. For decades, there has been recognition that everybody deserves access to the information they need to make an informed choice about their healthcare. But frequently, when a breastfeeding mother requires treatment with amedicine, that evidence simply does not exist.Studying drug safety and effectiveness in breastfeeding, so-called â€˜lactation pharmacologyâ€™, requires breastfeeding mothers to trust the research team, and for the research team to have the skills andequipment to perform research that keeps the number of participants and biological sampling points to a minimum whilst maximising the information gained. Once the research is complete, the research team must also engage with policy makers to make sure that the results change healthcare practice.AimsWe aim to meet the critical need for better understanding of which drugs are safe for mother and infant duringbreastfeeding by establishing of a centre of excellence for lactation pharmacology at the Infectious DiseasesInstitute in Uganda.1. To work with communities and decision-makers to understand which drugs we should study first2. To determine how to safely and fairly include in research breastfeeding mothers who have complexsituations, such as age 14-17, mental health conditions and breastfeeding during a virus outbreak3. To measure whether antidepressants and antibiotics pass to the infant through breastmilk4. To build mathematical prediction models to predict how likely it is that particular drugs will pass throughbreastmilk5. To be ready to explore safety and breastmilk transfer of new drugs during a virus outbreakIn parallel with this, we will:A. Work with local communitiesB. Train researchers in our methodsC. Work with policy makers to make sure our research changes healthcare
